findings: visitTwin is constructed within the actual crossing fiber: it retains v.1 and selects the other member of its support using crossing_other_visit. The canonical Crossing definition records a remote unordered edge pair and the proved crossing_card_two forces exactly two support members. No externally supplied involution, word pairing or geometric correspondence is a premise.

visitTwin_ne projects any alleged sigma equality to equality of the underlying edge labels and contradicts the chosen member's proved distinctness. visit_eq_or_twin uses crossing_visits_exhaust after identifying the crossing fibers, so it exhausts every actual visit of that crossing. visitTwin_unique then removes the original visit alternative.

visitTwin_involutive is derived from that uniqueness: v is the distinct other visit of visitTwin v. Therefore the chosen mate is independent of which existence witness Classical.choose uses. visitTwinPerm's inverse is exactly the constructed twin, with both inverse laws proved; no new pairing axiom is introduced.

selectedVisitTwin tests the actual crossing identity v.1 for membership in S. Selected visits are exchanged with their actual mates; unselected visits remain identical. Crossing identity is preserved, so membership is unchanged under a twin and selectedVisitTwin is an involution.

The empty support yields the identity function, and the fixed-point characterization is exact: selectedVisitTwin S v = v iff the crossing of v is not selected. A selected crossing cannot disappear through a fixed point because visitTwin_ne excludes that case.

The commutation theorem checks the four membership combinations for arbitrary supports S,T. Even an overlapping selected crossing causes two exchanges and hence returns the original visit in either order. The union/composition theorem correctly requires Disjoint S T, preventing the false claim that applying an overlapping exchange twice equals applying it once.
